apod.explanation: Saturn vanishes when the Moon passes in front of it — an occultation visible in early 2025 from Greenland through central Europe to northern Africa. This fusion of three images from Sardinia, Italy, catches Saturn just before it disappeared; the bright dot nearby is the star 85 Aquarii, and the next such occultation comes in 2031.
apod.title: Saturn Behind the Moon

breaking.headline: December hike now fully priced; Waller floats a half-point move
breaking.fact: Markets now price a December Fed hike at 100%, up from 82% Monday, after October CPI ran hot (+0.4% headline, +0.3% core) — and Gov. Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered if core inflation stays hot. Stocks are giving back part of Monday's rally and the 10-year is near 5.00%.

breaking.headline: Nvidia shareholders sue; Aletheia cuts to Hold as probe widens
breaking.fact: Shareholders filed a class action in San Jose federal court alleging Nvidia concealed CEO Jensen Huang's ties to a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy; Aletheia cut the stock to Hold, dropping its $340 target. About 600,000 H200 AI chips are sitting in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to China, and House leaders want a briefing from Huang on Nov 18. Shares are down about 6.5% today.

breaking.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price at $70–$78; Google, Nvidia to buy $26B
breaking.fact: The Claude maker launched its roadshow today with 825 million shares priced at $70–$78, raising up to $64.4B and valuing it at about $1T — $1.4T fully diluted. Google and Nvidia are each putting in $10B of a $26B private placement from seven tech firms; pricing is set for Nov 18, with trading expected Nov 19 under ticker ANT.

breaking.headline: TSMC October sales jump 60% to a record on AI demand
breaking.fact: The world's largest chipmaker posted October revenue of NT$586.89B (about $17.9B), up 59.7% year over year and 14.7% from September — a monthly record driven by 2-nanometer AI chip demand. Revenue for the first ten months is up 43.3%.

items.headline: Iranian forces strike navigation aids on Didamar Island
items.body: Iranian forces hit radar and navigation equipment on Didamar Island in the southern strait on Nov 9 and fired missiles at tankers in southern channels, per regional monitors. The IRGC claims three tankers were hit Nov 8; UKMTO confirmed two tanker incidents with no crew casualties. War-risk premiums for Gulf transit remain 0.85–1.10% of hull value, vs 0.05% before the crisis; the JMIC threat level is SEVERE.

items.headline: CENTCOM: strait open, 900M barrels moved since May
items.body: US Central Command says traffic 'continues to flow' under US naval coordination and that its forces have helped move more than 900 million barrels of crude through the strait since early May, while redirecting 122+ vessels under the blockade. AIS-visible traffic is still only about 8% of normal — 7.0 ships a day over the past week, including 19 tankers.

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 7.0 ships a day over the past week (19 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

marketsNote: Tuesday's session is giving back part of Monday's best day since April: hot October CPI (+0.4% headline, +0.3% core) has fully priced a December Fed hike — Waller even floated 50bp — and the 10-year is at 5.00%. S&P ~7,486 (-0.9%), Nasdaq ~24,930 (-1.3%), Dow ~52,047 (-0.7%); VIX 20.67. Oil extends its slide (WTI ~$86.69, Brent ~$91.98) as Trump plays down new Iran strikes. Bonds close tomorrow for Veterans Day while stocks trade; a $42B 10-year auction lands at 1:00 PM ET.

space.headline: Starship Flight 15 set for Friday; first dual catch attempt
space.body: SpaceX rolled Super Heavy Booster 22 to Pad 2 at Starbase ahead of Flight 15, targeted for Friday, Nov 13, in a window opening at 4:45 PM CT, pending FAA approval. It would be the first flight aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Starship upper stage back at the launch site; Ship 42 would orbit 14 times over about 22 hours.

space.headline: NASA to test two lunar landers in Earth orbit before 2028 landing
space.body: NASA's revised Artemis plan has Orion carrying four astronauts on Artemis III in 2027 to rendezvous and dock with test versions of both SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon landers in Earth orbit, before Artemis IV aims to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028. Which lander flies the crew depends on test results.

space.headline: 1,600-year-old Nazca burial holds a baby born with one central eye
space.body: DNA from a tiny skull in a Nazca urn at Jauranga, Peru (AD 325–440) shows the infant girl had trisomy 13, or Patau syndrome, which caused cyclopia — a single central eye socket. It is the first such case ever identified in an archaeological context, published Nov 9 in PNAS.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump declares Iran war 'effectively over'; strikes paused, blockade stays
weekInBrief.body: President Trump said the US-Iran war is 'effectively over' and that further strikes are paused pending diplomacy, after meeting Qatar's prime minister on Monday. The naval blockade and Operation Iron Gate remain in place, and Tehran disputes that talks exist. Oil slid on the news, with Brent falling below $92.

weekInBrief.headline: Oil extends its slide as Iran fears ease
weekInBrief.body: Brent crude is trading near $91.98 and WTI near $86.69 in late-morning trade, extending a slide that has taken Brent from $118 on Oct 30 and $97.00 on Monday. The drop follows Trump's signal that new strikes on Iran are unlikely; a $42B 10-year Treasury auction lands at 1:00 PM ET.

weekInBrief.headline: Federal debt at 101% of GDP, triple the 2001 level
weekInBrief.body: A new Congressional Research Service report puts publicly held federal debt at 101% of GDP at the end of fiscal 2026, more than triple the 32% recorded in 2001, the last surplus year. The CBO projects a fiscal 2026 deficit of $1.85 trillion (5.8% of GDP), with debt reaching 120% of GDP by 2036 and net interest at 4.6% of GDP.

weekInBrief.headline: Utility uranium contracting already outruns last year's pace
weekInBrief.body: Term uranium contracting so far this year tops 83 million pounds, against about 48 million at the end of October last year, as utilities lock in supply. Spot U3O8 is holding near $91/lb with the long-term price at $97/lb; Kazatomprom's Q3 realized price rose 18% to $81.50/lb, while the Sprott trust still trades at about a 16% discount to NAV.
